title: Finite-field curves admit a projective closure
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a field and let $U_0$ be an integral separated scheme of
finite type over $k_0$ of dimension at most one. There are an integer $N$,
a locally closed immersion $a:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{k_0}$,
and an integral projective scheme $X_0$ such that $a$ identifies
$U_0$ with a dense open subscheme of $X_0$, its scheme-theoretic
closure in $\mathbf P^N_{k_0}$.

proof.text: Convert the topological dimension bound from IsCurve to U.dim <= 1 using Scheme.dim_eq_topologicalKrullDim [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]. Apply [lem-sc-dim-one-quasi-projective] to get a closed immersion i:U -> V followed by an open immersion j:V -> projective space, both over the field; put a = i composed with j.

Projective space over the field is locally Noetherian. Factor the immersion a through its coborderRange; both the closed-immersion lift and the open inclusion into the locally Noetherian target are quasi-compact, hence a is quasi-compact. Take X = a.image, its scheme-theoretic image. The image inclusion a.imagei is a closed immersion, while a.toImage is an open immersion with dense image by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image].

Prove X integral without any new unproved lemma. The continuous image of the irreducible U under a.toImage is irreducible, and its closure is all of X by density, so X is irreducible. To prove reducedness, let s be a nilpotent section on an arbitrary open W of X. The preimages under a.imagei of affine opens V of projective space form a basis. On every such basis open inside W the map a.toImage.app is injective by Scheme.Hom.toImage_app_injective, as in [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image]. Its codomain is sections on an open of the integral U, hence reduced. Thus the restriction of s is zero; the sheaf section-extensionality theorem makes s zero on W. The Mathlib isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced theorem then proves X integral.

Choose n = ULift(Fin(N+1)), X = a.image, the closed immersion a.imagei, and the open immersion a.toImage. The identity a.toImage composed with a.imagei equals a, followed by associativity and the two structure-map identities of the chosen embedding, proves the required composite equals p. Density was supplied in step 2.

lean.statement:
theorem IsCurve.exists_projectiveClosure (p : U ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve p] [IsIntegral U] :
    ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (X : Scheme.{u}) (ι : X ⟶ ℙ(n; Spec (.of K))) (j : U ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion ι ∧ IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsIntegral X ∧ DenseRange j.base ∧
      j ≫ ι ≫ (ℙ(n; Spec (.of K)) ↘ Spec (.of K)) = p
lean.note: Existing source-library statement, now proved from the previously stated dimension-one quasi-projectivity theorem; the latter remains sorry.
